어울리다.m: to suit, to look good on; to go well with; to get along with
어울리다.x: That dress really looks good on you.
어울리다.t: "잘 어울려요!" is the go-to compliment when someone tries on clothes.

멀리.forms: 멀리 가다 · 멀리 살다; 멀리서 (from far away)
멀리.ex: 친구가 멀리 이사 가서 자주 못 만나요.
멀리.x: My friend moved far away, so I can't see her often.

관심.ex: 저는 요즘 한국 음악에 관심이 많아요.
관심.x: I'm really interested in Korean music these days.
관심.e: Literally 'the heart connected' — your mind is tied to something.
관심.t: Use the particle 에: 음악에 관심이 있어요 'I'm interested in music' — not 을/를.

다녀오다.m: to go and come back, to visit (and return)
다녀오다.x: Last week I went to Jeju Island with my family.
다녀오다.e: Built from 다니다 'to go around' + 오다 'to come': go and return.
다녀오다.t: Set phrases when leaving home: 다녀오겠습니다 'I'll be back' and 다녀오세요 'See you later.'

차다.m: to wear (a watch, belt); to kick
차다.x: My father always wears a wristwatch.
차다.e: Homonyms: other 차다 verbs mean 'to be full'; the adjective 차다 means 'cold'.
차다.t: Use 차다 for things worn at the wrist or waist: 시계를 차다, 벨트를 차다.

분홍색.x: My little sister likes pink dresses the most.
분홍색.e: Literally 'powder-red color', like pale red face powder.
분홍색.t: In casual speech many people just say 핑크 instead.

갈비.ex: 주말에 가족과 함께 갈비를 먹으러 갔어요.
갈비.x: On the weekend, I went out with my family to eat galbi.
갈비.e: Literally 'rib'; beef ribs are 소갈비, pork ribs are 돼지갈비.

쌍둥이.e: 쌍 'pair' plus native -둥이, a suffix for a kind of child.

뜨다.forms: 떠요 · 떴어요 · 뜰 거예요 · 뜨세요 (ㅡ drops)
뜨다.m: to rise (sun, moon); to float; to open (eyes)
뜨다.x: The sun rises around six in the morning.
뜨다.e: Several homonyms: 눈을 뜨다 'open eyes', 자리를 뜨다 'leave a seat'.
뜨다.t: Opposite pairs: 해가 뜨다 / 해가 지다, and 눈을 뜨다 / 눈을 감다.

숨다.ex: 아이가 숨바꼭질을 하면서 문 뒤에 숨었어요.
숨다.x: The child hid behind the door while playing hide-and-seek.
숨다.e: Found in 숨바꼭질 'hide-and-seek'; its causative 숨기다 means 'to hide something'.

따로.x: My friend and I paid separately.
따로.e: Doubled as 따로따로 for 'each one on its own'.

기한.x: The deadline for submitting the assignment has already passed.
기한.t: 유통기한 on food packages means 'expiration date'.

퇴원.x: Grandma's discharge date has been set.
퇴원.e: Literally 'leaving the institution'; the opposite is 입원, 'entering.'

안전.x: Please drive slowly for the children's safety.
안전.e: Literally 'peaceful and whole' — nothing broken, nothing harmed.
안전.t: Add 하다 for the adjective: 안전해요 means 'it's safe.'

우울하다.x: I feel down on rainy days.

도전하다.m: to challenge oneself, to take on, to try
도전하다.ex: 올해는 처음으로 마라톤에 도전해 보려고 해요.
도전하다.x: This year I'm going to try running a marathon for the first time.
도전하다.e: Literally 'provoke a fight'; now taking on any challenge.

소수.x: We should respect the opinions of the minority too.
소수.e: Literally 'few in number'; a different 소수 means 'decimal' in math.

투표하다.ex: 만 열여덟 살이 되면 선거에서 투표할 수 있어요.
투표하다.x: Once you turn eighteen, you can vote in elections.

규모.ex: 이번 축제는 작년보다 규모가 훨씬 커졌어요.
규모.x: This year's festival got much bigger in scale than last year's.
규모.e: Literally 'compass and mold': the frame that sets something's size.

단오.m: Dano (festival on the 5th day of the 5th lunar month)
단오.ex: 옛날에는 단오에 그네를 타고 씨름을 했어요.
단오.x: In the old days, people rode swings and wrestled on Dano.
단오.e: Held on the 5th day of the 5th lunar month; women washed their hair in iris water.

와이파이.ex: 이 카페에서는 와이파이를 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
와이파이.x: You can use the Wi-Fi for free at this café.
와이파이.t: To ask for the password, say 와이파이 비밀번호가 뭐예요?

화산.x: This island was formed when a volcano erupted.

대체 에너지.ex: 대체 에너지 개발이 점점 중요해지고 있어요.
대체 에너지.x: Developing alternative energy is becoming more and more important.

위선.x: If your words and actions differ, that's hypocrisy.

속이 좁다.forms: 속이 좁아요 · 속이 좁았어요 · 속이 좁은 사람
속이 좁다.m: to be petty, to be narrow-minded
속이 좁다.ex: 그런 작은 일로 화내다니 속이 좁네요.
속이 좁다.x: Getting angry over such a small thing is petty.
속이 좁다.e: Literally 'one's insides are narrow' — little room for others.

으레.forms: 으레 + habitual verb: 으레 ~곤 하다, 으레 ~는 법이다
으레.m: as a matter of course, habitually, naturally
으레.x: On weekends, my father would always go to the mountains.

의뢰하다.m: to request, to commission, to ask (a professional to do something)
의뢰하다.ex: 회사는 전문 변호사에게 이 사건을 의뢰했어요.
의뢰하다.x: The company hired a specialist lawyer to handle this case.
의뢰하다.e: Literally 'rely and depend' — entrusting a task to an expert.
의뢰하다.t: Used when asking professionals: 변호사, 전문가, 업체에 의뢰하다.

치우치다.m: to lean (to one side), be biased, be one-sided
치우치다.ex: 그 기사는 한쪽 의견에 너무 치우쳐 있어요.
치우치다.x: That article leans too heavily toward one side.

우왕좌왕.m: running around in confusion, not knowing what to do
우왕좌왕.ex: 불이 나자 건물 안의 사람들이 우왕좌왕했어요.
우왕좌왕.x: When the fire broke out, the people in the building ran around in confusion.

이념.ex: 두 정당은 정치 이념이 서로 달라요.
이념.x: The two parties have different political ideologies.
이념.e: Literally 'reasoned thought': a system of ideas.

대여.x: You can rent bikes at this park.

연습생.ex: 그 가수는 오 년 동안 연습생으로 지냈어요.
연습생.x: That singer spent five years as a trainee.
연습생.t: Pronounced [연습쌩]. K-pop trainees often train for years in singing, dancing and languages before they debut.

소극장.x: I saw a play at a small theater in Daehangno.
소극장.t: Pronounced [소극짱]. Seoul's 대학로 is packed with 소극장 showing plays and small musicals.

오타.x: I was writing in a hurry, so I made a lot of typos.
오타.t: A typo happens is 오타가 나다; fix one is 오타를 고치다/수정하다.

음치.m: tone-deaf person, someone who can't sing in tune
음치.x: I'm tone-deaf, so I get embarrassed when we go to karaoke.
음치.e: Literally 'sound fool'; -치 'fool' also gives 몸치 'bad dancer' and 길치 'someone with no sense of direction'.
음치.t: Usually said jokingly about oneself. Someone with no sense of rhythm is a 박치.

시효.ex: 그 사건은 이미 공소 시효가 지났습니다.
시효.x: The statute of limitations for that case has already expired.
시효.e: Literally 'effect of time' — a right that lapses after a period.
시효.t: Common phrase: 시효가 지나다 / 만료되다 (the limitation period expires).

은사.x: Twenty years after graduating, I visited my old high school teacher.
은사.e: Literally 'teacher of grace', a teacher you owe much to.
은사.t: Usually said with -님: 은사님; 찾아뵙다 is the humble verb for visiting them.

문체.x: That author is famous for his concise writing style.
문체.e: Literally 'writing body', the form a text takes.
문체.t: -체 also names speech styles and fonts: 해요체, 합니다체, 궁서체.

연출.m: directing, production (of a play, film or show); staging
연출.ex: 이 연극은 연출이 뛰어나서 관객들의 반응이 좋았어요.
연출.x: This play had excellent directing, so the audience reacted well.
연출.t: Film directors are usually 감독, while stage directors are 연출가; 연출 also means a staged or set-up scene.

아우르다.forms: 아울러요 · 아울렀어요 · 아우를 거예요 · 아우르세요 (르 irregular)
아우르다.m: to bring together, to embrace, to encompass
아우르다.ex: 그 가수의 노래는 세대를 아우르는 사랑을 받고 있어요.
아우르다.x: That singer's songs are loved across generations.
아우르다.e: The adverb 아울러 'in addition, together' comes from this verb.
아우르다.t: Common phrase: 세대를 아우르다 'to span generations.'

교묘하다.x: The con artist took the money in a crafty way.
교묘하다.t: Often negative: 교묘하게 속이다 'to cleverly deceive'.

살그머니.ex: 아기가 깰까 봐 살그머니 방문을 닫았어요.
살그머니.x: I quietly closed the door so the baby wouldn't wake up.
살그머니.e: Related to 살며시 and 슬그머니, all meaning 'softly, without being noticed'.

흥청망청.forms: 흥청망청 쓰다 · 흥청망청 마시다 · 흥청망청 놀다
흥청망청.m: extravagantly, wastefully; in a reckless, merrymaking way
흥청망청.ex: 월급을 흥청망청 쓰다가 월말에 돈이 하나도 없었어요.
흥청망청.x: I spent my paycheck recklessly and had no money left at the end of the month.
흥청망청.e: Rhyming doubled word; compare 흥청거리다 'to make merry, splash money around.'
흥청망청.t: Almost always with spending or partying: 돈을 흥청망청 쓰다 'to blow money.'

기로.m: crossroads, fork in the road (critical decision point)
기로.ex: 회사는 지금 생존이냐 몰락이냐의 기로에 서 있어요.
기로.x: The company now stands at a crossroads between survival and collapse.

전술.x: The coach switched to aggressive tactics in the second half.
전술.t: 전략 is big-picture strategy; 전술 is the specific tactics used to carry it out.

조제.t: Pharmacists 조제 (dispense) the medicine; doctors 처방 (prescribe) it.

설움.m: sorrow, grief (from hardship, neglect or mistreatment)
설움.ex: 그는 외국에서 혼자 살며 설움을 많이 겪었어요.
설움.x: Living alone abroad, he went through a lot of sorrow and hardship.
설움.e: Noun from 섧다 / 서럽다 'to feel sad and wronged'; 서러움 is a variant.

갈채.ex: 그의 연주가 끝나자 관객들은 뜨거운 갈채를 보냈습니다.
갈채.x: When his performance ended, the audience gave him warm applause.

어감.m: nuance, feel or connotation of a word
어감.ex: 두 단어는 뜻은 비슷하지만 어감이 달라요.
어감.x: The two words have similar meanings but a different feel.

뉘우치다.ex: 그는 자신의 잘못을 진심으로 뉘우치고 있어요.
뉘우치다.x: He sincerely repents of his mistake.
뉘우치다.e: Native Korean; implies moral remorse and wanting to change, deeper than simple regret.
뉘우치다.t: Usually takes 잘못 or 죄 as its object: 잘못을 뉘우치다.

고뇌.ex: 그 결정에는 오랜 고뇌가 담겨 있었습니다.
고뇌.x: That decision came out of long anguish.

처연하다.ex: 비 오는 날 혼자 앉아 있는 그의 모습이 처연했어요.
처연하다.x: The sight of him sitting alone on the rainy day was heartbreaking.
처연하다.e: Literally 'in a sorrowful state'; mostly literary.
처연하다.t: Literary: usually describes a scene, look or atmosphere rather than your own feelings.

뒤숭숭하다.m: to be uneasy, unsettled; restless (of mood or atmosphere)
뒤숭숭하다.ex: 이상한 꿈을 꿔서 하루 종일 기분이 뒤숭숭했어요.
뒤숭숭하다.x: I had a weird dream, so I felt uneasy all day.
뒤숭숭하다.e: A mimetic word suggesting things jumbled and messy; also used for a tense social mood.
뒤숭숭하다.t: Common collocations: 꿈자리가 뒤숭숭하다 (bad dreams), 분위기가 뒤숭숭하다 (tense atmosphere).

소묘.ex: 미대 입시를 준비하면서 매일 소묘를 연습했어요.
소묘.x: While preparing for art school entrance exams, I practiced drawing every day.
소묘.e: Literally 'plain depiction' — line and shading without color.
소묘.t: 소묘 and 데생 mean the same thing; 소묘 sounds a bit more formal.
